svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: The agent turns its own reasoning into an Arcgram, self-audits it for logic / data holes, Bug Marks each hole
and fixes them — then the human views the flow to decide.
hand the data to the engine
mark each hole on its node
the flow, holes shown on nodes
red = the agent working loop (Step 1 to 5)
bold gold = hand-off to the human
amber = feedback loop back to the agent
The agent reaches a proposed plan / design / decision. Normally this would stay as prose.
The agent takes its reasoning as data and hands it to the Arcgram engine to draw.
Reads the produced flow back as data and checks for data / logic holes: orphan step, dead goal, missing link, unhandled branch, contradiction.
Each hole found gets a red Bug Mark on the specific node, with a note.
Revise the plan / data to close each hole, re-draw, re-audit. Repeat until clean.
The authoring contract: what a node / edge / band is, and how to lay a flow out. What the agent follows when it draws.
Auto-layout + orthogonal routing + render into a single standalone HTML. No build, no runtime. The agent data passes through here to become the flow.
The coherence validator (orphans, islands, code to diagram) plus the geometry gates. The instruments the self-audit runs.
Marks a hole on a node and tracks it found to resolved.
One standalone HTML — human-readable AND agent-readable. Pan / zoom / hover. Produced by the engine from the agent data.
The same flow, now carrying the Bug Marks — each open hole shown on its node.
Holes resolved. A diagram that is both a communication artifact and a verification artifact.
The user views the diagram and gives a decision or feedback to the agent: approve, redirect, or point at a remaining gap. The key human-in-the-loop moment.
